cues.zh: 如果你被人跟踪，或是家庭暴力的受害者，想把自己的信息

cues.zh: 从这些搜人网站上抹去，完全合情合理。但遗憾的是，

cues.en: each has its own specific and sometimes very complex process of requesting the removal of information, and there is no federal law requiring that they honor an opt out request at all. And the lack of regulation here doesn't just benefit individuals
cues.zh: 每家网站都有各自甚至极其繁琐的信息删除流程，而且根本没有联邦法律强制要求它们必须配合退出申请。这种监管缺失，受益的不仅是那些

cues.en: who might mean you harm. It benefits the government too because it gives them a very attractive loophole to the Fourth Amendment protection against unreasonable searches and seizures because under that, the government typically needs a warrant to collect information about you without your consent.
cues.zh: 可能想伤害你的人。政府也同样获益，因为这给他们提供了一个极具诱惑力的漏洞，借此绕过第四修正案对不合理搜查和扣押的保护——毕竟在宪法规定下，未经同意收集你的信息，政府通常需要搜查令。

cues.en: But if it is not forcing someone to turn over your data, if it's simply buying it from a data broker,
cues.zh: 但如果政府不是强迫某人交出你的数据，而只是从数据掮客那里买下来，

cues.en: that is apparently fine. No warrant necessary.
cues.zh: 这显然就合规了。根本不需要搜查令。

cues.en: And you can see how valuable that would be to them. It happens all the time. In fact, federal agencies from the FBI to ICE have purchased data without warrants, public disclosures, or robust oversight to carry out everything from criminal investigations to deportations.
cues.zh: 你能想象这对他们有多大价值。这种情况随时都在发生。事实上，从 FBI 到 ICE 等各联邦机构，都在没有搜查令、缺乏公开披露或有效监管的情况下大肆购买数据，用于执行从刑事侦查到驱逐出境等各类任务。

cues.en: And the thing is, you might not know if your information has been supplied to the government by an app. Even the company behind the app might not know because it might sell your info to a broker, which then resells it to someone else, which then supplies it to the government. I'll give you an example. A couple years back, Vice found that the app Muslim Pro, which lets Muslims know when to pray, have been selling user location data to a broker that supplied information to the US government. And while because the chain is so opaque, it is hard to know what exactly was sold or what the government did with it, the app's users were understandably
cues.zh: 问题还在于，你的信息是否被某个应用提供给了政府，你可能一无所知。甚至应用背后的开发公司都未必知情，因为它可能把你的信息卖给了一家掮客，掮客转卖给下家，下家再提供给政府。我举个例子。几年前 Vice 发现，为穆斯林提供祈祷时间提醒的应用 Muslim Pro，一直在把用户位置数据卖给一家掮客，而该掮客正向美国政府供应数据。尽管由于交易链条极不透明，很难查清到底卖了什么或政府拿去做了什么，但该应用的用户自然是

cues.zh: 感到不安、

cues.en: appalled,
cues.zh: 骇人听闻，

cues.zh: 但并不意外。Sarah Mustafa 之前就用过 Muslim Pro。据报道，该应用后来已与数据合作伙伴切断了联系。侵犯性实在太强了。

cues.en: You know, my conversation with God
cues.zh: 要知道，我和上帝的对话

cues.en: is not information that the government needs.
cues.zh: 可不是政府应该掌握的信息。

cues.en: So to recap here, we've got shady data brokers with virtually no oversight, collecting your data and building profiles that can track who you are, where you are, and what you are most likely to do or buy. You cannot edit this dossier, and others from cops to reporters to your own abusers can find and use this information.
cues.zh: 总结一下，这里有一群几乎不受任何监管的暗盘数据掮客，他们在收集你的数据并建立画像，追踪你是谁、在哪儿，以及你最可能做什么或买什么。你无法修改这份档案，而其他人——从警察、记者到侵害你的人——都能找到并利用这些信息。

cues.en: It's not a great situation.
cues.zh: 现状并不太妙。

cues.en: So what do we do? Well, it is a bit tricky,
cues.zh: 那我们该怎么办？呃，这确实有点棘手，

cues.en: especially given the fact that the entire economy of the Internet right now is basically built on this practice.
cues.zh: 尤其是考虑到，如今整个互联网经济基本都建立在这一套玩法之上。

cues.en: All the free stuff that you take for granted online is only free because you are the product. They make money by selling your data. But experts say that there are actually some small steps that you can personally take. You can use web browsers like these to help better protect you against third party tracking. And if you have an iPhone, you can go to the privacy menu, hit the tracking button, and turn off allow apps to request to track. But this should not be your responsibility.
cues.zh: 你在网上习以为常的所有免费服务之所以免费，是因为你本身就是产品。他们靠出卖你的数据来赚钱。但专家表示，个人其实还是可以采取一些小措施的。你可以使用这类浏览器来更好地防范第三方追踪。如果你用的是 iPhone，可以进入隐私设置，点击跟踪选项，然后关闭“允许 App 请求跟踪”。但这本不该是你的责任。

cues.en: Your privacy should be the default setting here, and there should be legal fixes to this. Other countries have actually tried. The EU passed a law to force sites to disclose cookies and allow you to opt out.
cues.zh: 保护隐私本来就该是默认设置，而且应当有法律手段来解决。其他国家其实已经尝试过了。欧盟就通过了一项法律，强制网站披露 Cookie 并允许用户选择退出。

No one is gonna put in the work to reject cookies
